device.model: TP9012, TP920, TP940, TP960/962/968 (TempSpike), TP980, TP426 (plain BLE GATT series)
device.name: ThermoPro TempSpike / TP9xx BBQ Thermometer
device.notes:
Extracted from com.thermopro.thermopro v1.21 (48MB, TempPro APKPure XAPK).
Decompiled: 14,930 classes. Package: cn.com.adsmart.wifibbq.
Adsmart is the OEM behind ThermoPro's connected devices.

TRANSPORT IS PLAIN BLE GATT — NOT BLE MESH. The app contains no mesh stack
(no/nordicsemi/android/ holds only ble/ + support/; no Mesh Proxy 0x1828,
no PB-GATT, no provisioning anywhere in the sources). Two independent RE
efforts agree: daniel-corbett/thermopro-cli calls it "a simple BLE
notification-based protocol", and Bluetooth-Devices/thermopro-ble decodes
TempSpike probes passively from advertisements with no connection at all.
An earlier revision of this spec describing BLE Mesh provisioning was
fabricated.

THERE IS NO SINGLE UNIVERSAL UUID SET. The app picks one of FIVE
per-family BLE configs at connect time (MyBleManager.java:103-128,
ble/config/*Config.java; 16-bit codes expand to
0000XXXX-0000-1000-8000-00805F9B34FB via UUIDUtil):
- TP9012 family (deviceType 7/8, TP90XConfig): service
  0B863E05-BA64-4F7A-922D-007FD52DCAA9 — NOT 1086FFF0 — write FFF1,
  notify FFF2.
- TP922 (deviceType 22, TP922Config): service
  BAAAFFF0-0001-4E6E-886A-57D347C919FE, write BAAAFFF1-…, notify
  BAAAFFF2-….
- TP940 (deviceType 24) and TempSpike TP960 (deviceTypes 30/31):
  service 93bb7cab-eb14-c5a9-2354-a24f4df9330f with roles REVERSED —
  write = FF02, notify = FF01 — plus a read characteristic FF03.
- TP426 infrared (deviceType 50): service
  0F86FFF0-63E8-4762-9DFB-7B6FE113376A, write FFF1, notify FFF2.
- Default (all other deviceTypes, incl. TP920/TP25W and TP980,
  TPBleConfig): service 1086FFF0-3343-4817-8BB2-B32206336CE8, write
  FFF1, notify FFF2.
Clients must identify the family (advertised name, per ScanConfig.java)
before choosing a service; 1086FFF0 is the fallback, not the universal
case.

WRITE FRAMING IS PER-FAMILY. Only the TP9012 family wraps commands as
0xAA | payload | checksum | 0xFF, where checksum = sum of the payload
bytes EXCLUDING the opcode byte, & 0xFF (TP9012Data.getIntCheckSum);
its notifications mirror this with 0xAA at offset 0 and the opcode at
offset 1. TP920/TP25W-family frames have NO 0xAA/0xFF wrapper and a
trailing checksum that INCLUDES the opcode byte
(TP920Data.getIntCheckSum:247-258); this family additionally expects a
fixed init handshake write (starting 01 09 8a 7a ...) plus a
timestamp-sync command 0x28 after connect (thermopro-cli
create_handshake_command). TP940, TP960 (TempSpike) and TP980 send raw
opcode-prefixed frames with NO wrapper and NO checksum at all
(TP940Data/TP960Data/TP980Data build Data straight from the opcode
bytes).

Eight device change-utility families are dispatched in the app
(MyBleManager.notificationDataCallback): TP9012, TP920, TP940, TP960,
TP962, TP968, TP980 and TP426 (infrared). The TempSpike line
(TP960/962/968 and TP970-973) is the current retail focus.

TEMPSPIKE PASSIVE MODE: TP96x/TP97x probes broadcast probe index,
temperatures and battery voltage in BLE advertisement manufacturer data
(company id prepended LE by the parser) — fully decodable without
connecting (Bluetooth-Devices/thermopro-ble parser.py, actively
maintained). This is the cheapest integration path for those models and
obviates most of the setup below. TWO DIFFERENT LAYOUTS EXIST — an
earlier revision of this spec claimed "°F + 54 offset" for all of them,
which is wrong for TP96x:
- TP96x / TP970 (7-byte payload; a 13-byte variant appends 6 bytes —
  observed to be the reversed base-station MAC — which are ignored):
  "<BHHH" = probe_index u8, internal_temp u16, battery_voltage u16,
  ambient_temp u16. Temperatures are INTEGER values with a -30 offset
  (raw - 30), NOT °F (parser.py:184-206).
- TP97x (23-byte payload): "<BHHfffHHH" = probe_index u8, ambient_temp
  u16, battery_voltage u16, then three float32 internal temperatures
  (tip/center/end), three u16 ignored. Only THIS family encodes temps
  as float32 °F with a +54 offset: celsius = (raw - 54 - 32) * 5/9 —
  the same fahrenheit_to_celsius(x - 54) the connected TP980 path uses
  (parser.py:155-182).
Battery from advertisements uses a fitted tanh curve (mV → %):
52.317286 * tanh(v/273.624277936 - 8.76485439394) + 51.06925, clamped
0-100 (tp96_battery).

FIRMWARE/DFU: the app carries TWO OTA paths (ble/config/DfuConfig.java,
OtaConfig.java). There is a DFU-mode GATT service 0x1850 (write 0x2C00,
notify 0x2C01), and two vendor OTA profiles with bundled firmware
images: ASR560X (service 0917fe11-5d37-816d-8000-00805f9b34fb, write
09170001-…, notify 09170002-…; bundled res/raw/ast6s53_v25_ota.bin,
version 2.5, string app-2.5.0-20251011.1000, archived in the research
store — TempSpike-era hardware is ASR560X-based, not Nordic) and
Silicon Labs (OTA service 1d14d6ee-fd63-4fa1-bfa4-8f47b42119f0, control
f7bf3564-fb6d-4e53-88a4-5e37e0326063, write
984227f3-34fc-4045-a5d0-2c581f81a153; bundled
res/raw/ota_hpyke25_2101_v117, version 1.17). Images are pushed to
devices over BLE by OTAUtil/OtaConfig.

ThermoPro is rebranding to "TempPro" (announced ~April 2026; temppro.com);
the app already references both buythermopro.com and temppro.com.

credentials.notes: No credential protects the BLE link itself — any central can connect and exchange commands. WiFi/cloud binding is NOT TP980-only: TP980 (scan name TP980R, the app's "tempWifi" group) uses notification opcodes decimal 80-84 = 0x50-0x54 (an earlier revision of this spec wrote "0x80-0x84", confusing decimal with hex) for wifiScan/wifiConnect/wifiCheck and cloud binding, returning the WiFi MAC, an 18-char device did and boundUser; the TP920/TP25W family has the same capability on opcodes 0x60-0x67 (writes: scanWifi 0x60, connectWifi 0x62, checkWifi 0x63, unBound 0x64, checkDid 0x66; notifications: wifiScanReturn 0x61, wifiConnectReturn 0x63/0x67, boundNotification 0x65, checkDidReturn 0x66 — TP920Data.java:193-244, TP920DataChangeUtils.java:60). Unlike the TP980 set, no decimal/hex confusion applies to these: the decompiled literals are decimal 96-103, which equal hex 0x60-0x67 exactly as written here. The apparent write/notify overlaps are real request/response opcode sharing — the device's reply notification echoes the request's opcode (checkWifi write 0x63 → wifiConnectReturn notify 0x63, checkDid write 0x66 → checkDidReturn notify 0x66; 0x61 and 0x65 likewise double as the client's ack writes wifiScanReturn(index) and returnUnBoundDevice), while 0x67 is a notification-only WiFi connect-state variant with no matching write. So a WiFi passphrase IS involved for those families, and TP980W is sold as a Wi-Fi model. No TP980 cloud broker endpoint is identifiable from static code; the binding rides the device did.
stored_on_device: WiFi families (TP980, TP920/TP25W): WiFi credentials + 18-char device id (did) / cloud binding

factory_reset.effect: No factory-reset button sequence was established from the app or any public source. Consult the model's manual rather than guessing.

methods.description: Scan for the advertised name (TP940R, TP980R, TP960R, Thermopro, SmartBBQ, ... per ScanConfig.java), identify the family from the name, connect to the family's service (see the five configs in device.notes — 1086FFF0-… is only the default for TP920/TP980 and others, write FFF1 / notify FFF2; TP940/TP960 use 93bb7cab-… with write FF02 / notify FF01; TP9012-family uses 0B863E05-…), enable notifications, and — on the TP920/TP25W/TP904 family — write the fixed handshake (01 09 8a 7a ...) plus timestamp sync (command 0x28) before issuing commands.

steps.action: Power the thermometer on; it advertises immediately.
Scan for the advertised name and identify the family; the service UUID in the device's own advertisement distinguishes it (1086FFF0 is the default, not the universal case).
Connect to the family's service, enable notifications on its notify characteristic, and send the family handshake where required.

Exchange commands in the family's framing (0xAA|payload|checksum|0xFF only on TP9012; checksum-including-opcode on TP920; raw opcodes on TP940/TP960/TP980) — or, on TempSpike models, just parse the advertisements.

setup.notes:
Plain BLE GATT: scan, identify the family (the UUID set and framing are per-family — see device.notes), connect, subscribe to the family's notify characteristic, run the short init handshake where the family requires it, then exchange opcode-prefixed commands. There is no provisioning, no pairing and no mesh layer. For TempSpike TP96x/TP97x models even the connection is optional — temperatures and battery arrive passively in advertisements.
Confidence is medium: the flows are read from the decompiled app and two independent RE projects, but have not been run against a device here.

rejoin.notes: Nothing binds the thermometer to a BLE client: no keys, no pairing, no account. Switching controllers is scanning and connecting from the new one. (The WiFi families — TP980 and TP920/TP25W — additionally hold WiFi credentials and a vendor-cloud binding for their uplink — that binding is between the device and the cloud, not the BLE client.)

4-probe (+ambient slot) BBQ thermometer with meat temperature settings
device_families.protocol_notes:
Per-probe push notifications (tempReturn opcodes 0x61/0x10, probe index
in byte 1) — there is NO polling state machine on this family; the
setTemp(0..3) sequential-probing flow belongs to TP980. Other opcodes:
0x02 unit, 0x04 alarm setting, 0x05 alarm close, 0x06 device close,
0x67 color. Battery: raw×33 for both probes and box
(TP940ChangeUtils.java:81,97,117) — note this is the INVERSE of the
TP9012 formula (100 − 33×raw).
device_families.temperature_encoding_detail: BCD: temp = (b1>>4)*100 + (b1&0x0F)*10 + (b2>>4) + (b2&0x0F)*0.1 °C; negative when the high nibble of b1 is 0x9 (subtract 1000). Disconnect sentinel 0xCC,0xCC → -999.0 (TP940ChangeUtils.getProTemp). The TP920/ TP25W family uses the same BCD digit layout but DIFFERENT sign/sentinel handling — sign = bit 0x80 of b1, sentinels 0xFF,0xFF → -999.0 / 0xDD,0xDD → -100.0 / 0xEE,0xEE → 666.0 (TP920DataChangeUtils. getProTemp:654-665) — which is also the scheme thermopro-cli's decode_temperature implements, so the CLI is a valid reference for TP920 but NOT for TP940's sign/sentinels. TempSpike TP96x does not use BCD at all (u16 LE − 30, see the TP960 family below).

device_families.description: TempSpike wireless single-probe spike + base station — the current retail focus (scan names TP960R, TP960W, I61, I61W)
device_families.protocol_notes:
CONNECTED-MODE opcodes (spec previously had no TP96x GATT block despite
being named "tempspike"). Service 93bb7cab-…, write FF02 / notify FF01,
raw frames with NO checksum. Notifications (opcode at offset 0,
TP960ChangeUtils.java:90-91): 0x01 current temp, 0x02 history upload
first frame, 0x05 low battery upload, 0x06 box battery upload, 0x10
auto temp return, 0x11 low battery (alt), 0x12 probe connect upload,
0x13 temp alarm close, 0x14 ambient temp alarm close. Writes
(TP960Data): 0x01 read temp, 0x02 read temp history, 0x03 auto-
notification on/off, 0x04 set probe temp alarm (°C and °F variants),
0x05 read battery state, 0x06 read battery (TP962), 0x15 set ambient
temperature alarm, 0x19 set temp unit, 0x1A read probe color. Battery:
u16 LE millivolt bands <2311 → 0%, 2311-2450 → 33%, 2451-2600 → 66%,
≥2601 → 100% (TP960ChangeUtils.getBattery:255-263); passive ads use the
fitted tanh curve instead (see device.notes).
device_families.temperature_encoding_detail: Connected mode: u16 LE minus 30 °C (temp = raw - 30; TP960ChangeUtils.getProTemp:242+) — the SAME encoding as the TP96x passive-advertisement layout, NOT the TP940 BCD scheme. Sentinels: 0xFF,0xFF → -999.9, and raw - 30 ≤ -30 → -999.9. Passive mode layout per TEMPSPIKE PASSIVE MODE in device.notes.

device_families.description: TempSpike multi-probe variants (scan names TP962R, TP963, TP965R, TP966R)
device_families.protocol_notes:
Same service/framing as TP960 but a WIDER notification dispatch
(TP962ChangeUtils.java:95-115, TP968ChangeUtils.java) adding a
sequential setTemp-probing state machine: 0x81 readNextProTemp,
0x04/0x84 setTempReturn, 0x06/0x16 box battery, 0x09/0x89 setUnitReturn,
plus 0x10 auto temp, 0x12 probe connect, 0x13/0x14 alarm close, 0x17
charge state change, 0x18 device close, 0x19 temp unit change, 0x1A
probe color check.
device_families.temperature_encoding_detail: Same u16 LE − 30 °C encoding as TP960 (TP962ChangeUtils.getProTemp, TP968ChangeUtils.getProTempC/getProTemp); sentinel 0xFF,0xFF → -999.9.

device_families.description: Pro-grade 4-probe thermometer with history upload and WiFi uplink (TP980/TP980W sold as Wi-Fi + Bluetooth models)
device_families.protocol_notes:
History upload: multi-chunk transfer with a first frame (opcode 0x02)
and continuation frames, 6 bytes/record. Probe reading uses the
setTemp(0..3) / readNextProTemp sequential state machine
(TP980ChangeUtils — an earlier revision of this spec misattributed it
to TP940). Notification opcodes (TP980ChangeUtils.java:115): 0x11 temp
return, 0x12 probe connect, 0x13 temp alarm close, 0x14 ambient temp
alarm close, 0x17 charge state change, 0x18 device close, 0x19 temp
unit change, 0x1A probe color check, 0x20 temp auto-return, and
decimal 80-84 = 0x50-0x54 for WiFi scan/connect/check plus cloud
binding (did, boundUser). Battery: u16 LE millivolt bands <2311 → 0%,
2311-2450 → 33%, 2451-2600 → 66%, ≥2601 → 100%
(TP980ChangeUtils.getBattery:477-484).
device_families.temperature_encoding_detail: IEEE 754 float32 read LITTLE-ENDIAN (Nordic Data.FORMAT_UINT32) at offsets 5/9/13 (tp980TempReturn). The wire value is °F with a +54 offset: convert via fToC(raw - 54) — the same fahrenheit_to_celsius(x - 54) the thermopro-ble parser applies for TP97x.

characteristics.description: Client → device command channel. Framing is per-family: on TP920 frames carry a trailing checksum that INCLUDES the opcode (no 0xAA/0xFF wrapper); on TP980 frames are raw opcode bytes with no checksum. This is a custom vendor service — NOT the BLE Mesh Proxy service (that would be 0x1828); there is no mesh anywhere in this product.
